chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: Demarcate the modern periodic table into s and p block. Which law determines this demarcation?
keyPoints: ["s block: Groups 1–2","p block: Groups 13–18 except He","Periodic law"]
modelAnswer: The s block contains Groups 1 and 2, whose valence electrons enter an s subshell. The p block contains Groups 13–18 (except He), whose valence electrons enter a p subshell. Their placement follows the periodic law, in which properties repeat with increasing atomic number.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: Recognize and justify the presence of more similar chemical properties among Li, Na, K and Li, C, F.
keyPoints: ["Same group and valence configuration for Li/Na/K","Different groups/configurations for Li/C/F"]
modelAnswer: Li, Na and K are in the same Group 1 and have the same one-electron valence-shell pattern, so they have similar chemical properties. Li, C and F are in different groups with different valence-shell configurations, so their chemical properties are not as similar.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: Differentiate between period and group in the periodic table.
keyPoints: ["Period: horizontal row","Group: vertical column/family","Same-group elements have similar chemical properties"]
modelAnswer: A period is a horizontal row in the periodic table; a group is a vertical column or family. Elements in a group have similar valence-electron configurations and chemical properties, while the period number corresponds to the principal shell being filled.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: Briefly describe ionization energy and electron affinity along with their trends in groups and periods.
keyPoints: ["Ionization energy definition and trends","Electron affinity definition and trends"]
modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the minimum energy needed to remove the outermost electron from an isolated gaseous atom; it generally decreases down a group and increases across a period. Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added to an isolated atom to form a uni-negative ion; it generally decreases down a group and increases across a period.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: How do atomic size, ionization energy and electronegativity vary down the group?
keyPoints: ["Atomic size increases","Ionization energy decreases","Electronegativity decreases"]
modelAnswer: Down a group, atomic size increases because an additional electron shell is added. Ionization energy decreases because shielding increases and the outer electron is easier to remove. Electronegativity generally decreases because the valence shell is farther from the nucleus and more shielded.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: Briefly explain the difference in ionization energies of alkali and alkaline earth metals.
keyPoints: ["Alkali metals: one valence electron/+1","Alkaline earth metals: two valence electrons/+2","Ionization energy decreases down a group"]
modelAnswer: Alkali metals have one valence electron and form +1 ions; alkaline-earth metals have two valence electrons and generally require more energy to remove the first electron because their effective nuclear attraction is greater. In both families, ionization energy decreases down the group as shielding and atomic size increase.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: Periodic trends of Group IIA atomic size, ionization energy, electronegativity.
keyPoints: ["Atomic size increases down Group IIA","Ionization energy decreases down Group IIA","Electronegativity decreases down Group IIA"]
modelAnswer: Down Group IIA, atomic size increases because additional electron shells are added. Ionization energy decreases because shielding increases and the outer electron is easier to remove. Electronegativity generally decreases because the valence shell is farther from the nucleus and more shielded.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: Predict the trend of atomic size, ionization energy and electronegativity of Group IIA using knowledge of chemical periodicity.
keyPoints: ["Atomic size increases","Ionization energy decreases","Electronegativity decreases"]
modelAnswer: As Group IIA is descended, atomic size increases because a new shell is added. Ionization energy decreases because shielding weakens the nucleus–valence-electron attraction. Electronegativity also generally decreases as the valence electrons become farther from the nucleus.

stem: Give any two displacement reactions of halogens.
keyPoints: ["Chlorine oxidizes/displaces bromide","Chlorine oxidizes/displaces iodide"]
modelAnswer: Cl2 + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br2; Cl2 + 2KI → 2KCl + I2. Chlorine displaces bromide and iodide because it is the stronger oxidizing halogen than Br2 and I2.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: Predict Cl2 reactions with Br− and I−.

modelAnswer: Chlorine displaces both bromide and iodide: Cl2 + 2Br− → 2Cl− + Br2 and Cl2 + 2I− → 2Cl− + I2. Chlorine is the stronger oxidizing halogen in each pair.

chapterTitle: Periodic Table And Periodicity Of Properties
stem: Predict reactions of Cl2 with Br- and I- halide ions.
keyPoints: ["Cl2 displaces Br−","Cl2 displaces I−"]
modelAnswer: Cl2 + 2Br− → 2Cl− + Br2; Cl2 + 2I− → 2Cl− + I2. Chlorine oxidizes and displaces both bromide and iodide because it is higher in the halogen oxidizing-power order.
